track: The Agent That Can Explain Why
verification: Submitted badge and Submitted 1 / 1 persisted after reload; no server submission timestamp was displayed.
description:
TraceHarbor helps operations analysts turn disputed shipment temperature alerts into cited, inspectable explanations and next steps.

An alarm can disagree with a carrier status, and decisive evidence may be buried in calibration records or missing observations. TraceHarbor connects manifests, telemetry, carrier events and calibration through Zetaris and the official Meterless World Model. A Nightshift planner chooses initial evidence; a critic can retrieve omitted sources and test the result by withholding support; a constrained synthesis returns supported findings.

In a verified local TH-1042 investigation, manifest and telemetry alone led to abstention. The critic retrieved calibration and incidents, revealing sensor bias: a raw 10.1°C peak corrected to 5.6°C under a confirmed +4.5°C offset, with agreeing reference observations. Withholding calibration restored abstention. A separate incomplete-record case remained unresolved.

The responsive workspace exposes source rows, contradictions, coverage-aware charts, evidence experiments and exportable dossiers. Four original synthetic scenarios, 33 passing tests, a clean-clone check and archived live execution support the prototype.

The public demo is a deterministic sample; real local sponsor runs have separate receipts. We aim to reduce manual reconciliation and improve handoffs, but have not measured customer impact. TraceHarbor does not authorize cargo release or certify safety.

Team: Seyed Mohammad Salehi (@madvidd) — project lead, implementation, integrations, UI/UX, documentation, deployment and primary contact. Ali Rajaee — testing.

Public demo: https://traceharbor.web.app
sponsor_technology_explanation:
Zetaris supplies the evidence data layer. We registered four synthetic REST feeds for manifests, telemetry, carrier events and calibration; executed 12 source-exploration queries; compiled and activated a four-table shipment-evidence USL; and ran telemetry_integrity, which found 26 rows: 25 valid and one invalid 999°C observation. The live agent executes allowlisted USL reads rather than model-generated SQL. These feeds represent distinct operational systems on one demonstration host, not four independent production providers.

The official Meterless World Model powers structured evidence context. Our wrapper ingests source rows, reconstructs evidence from graph context, and persists source-priority facts and the final verdict. Each final live run consumed 46 evidence records, with engine events and audit logs retained. Its upstream conformance checks passed 8/8.

Meterless Nightshift is the primary provider for all three live model phases: planner, critic and synthesis. These are distinct constrained roles using the same local Llama 3.2 1B Instruct model. The critic actually retrieved omitted incidents and calibration through Zetaris, changing an unresolved TH-1042 result into sensor bias; withholding calibration restored abstention. A second current case retained insufficient evidence. Both current runs made three real model calls and four SQL reads. Budgets cap each run at three model calls, four unique reads and five minutes. A failed live run never silently substitutes sample output; earlier failed attempts remain archived.

Our original work includes the interface, evidence calculations, orchestration, integration wrappers, SQL setup, synthetic fixtures, tests and presentation material. Pre-existing components are the official World Model at revision 1742dec56a66e58eef9dda2d2b865823758ca8cd (Apache-2.0; notices retained), standard React/Vite and other licensed dependencies, and the repository's original MIT LICENSE and short README scaffold. OpenAI Codex assisted development. No NVIDIA/Nemotron, Cursor or SpaceX AI contribution is claimed.

The published Firebase site is explicitly a deterministic sample. Actual local sponsor execution, generated traces, matching browser exports, 33 passing tests and clean-clone results are independently inspectable in the public repository: https://github.com/madvidd/GenAI.works_Hackathon
